fields.h1: Build Game Survey Questions and Act on the Answers
fields.hero_description: Build game survey questions for playtests and game nights, with every answer saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Game Survey Built by Emergent Handles
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the questions and the app that runs them, with skip logic and an alert when a result crosses your line.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted for your game

Describe the game, the players, and the decision the answers feed. Emergent drafts the rating, ranking, and open questions, and a follow-up prompt rewrites any one of them.
fields.feature_2:
Questions that follow the player

The survey branches on earlier answers. A tester who quit at level 6 skips every question about level 10 and rates only the levels they played, with no blank rows to clean up.
fields.feature_3:
One question per screen on a phone

Players answer one question per screen on a phone, between rounds or on the bus home. A difficulty rating is a single tap, and an open answer gets a full-width text box.
fields.feature_4:
Answers tagged by build or session

Every response is a row in a database you own, tagged with the build number or the session date. Compare level 9 on build 14 with build 15 without merging two spreadsheets.
fields.feature_5:
An alert when a threshold is crossed

Set a threshold, such as half the testers rating a level 5 for difficulty. The designer gets a Slack or email alert when it is crossed, with the level and the count.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, your code, no response cap

Host the survey on your own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. Responses have no cap, and on paid plans the full code exports to your GitHub repository.

fields.tab_content_1:
Level 9 gets 3 more moves after 34 testers call it too hard

Quillbright Games sends a playtest survey to the 60 testers of Reefshine, its tile-matching puzzle game. Each tester rates every level they reached on a 5-point difficulty scale. Of the 52 who answer, 34 rate level 9 a 5. The designer adds 3 moves to level 9 before the next build goes out.
fields.tab_content_2:
The cafe gives its Thursdays to co-op games

Rollhaven Board Game Cafe has a free night each week and no plan for it. Its survey asks which night each member comes in and which kind of game they reach for first. It goes to 140 members, and 96 answer. Of those, 44 pick Thursday, and co-op games lead with 38 votes. Thursday becomes co-op night.
fields.tab_content_3:
Exploration ranked first before the campaign starts

Five players sit down for the first Ember Hollow session on Friday. The game master's session zero survey has each player rank combat, roleplay, and exploration, then list topics to keep out of the game, saved without names. Exploration comes first for 4 of 5 players, so the first arc is mapping a sunken city.
fields.tab_content_4:
A party game board written by 84 coworkers

A week before the Wexmoor Supply holiday party, 84 staff answer 8 open questions, such as something people forget at the office. The host merges near matches like charger and phone charger. The top 5 answers to each question go on the game board, and phone charger leads with 29 of 84.

fields.howto_title: How to Write Game Survey Questions
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write game survey questions that players finish and that end in a clear decision about the game.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Keep one scale for every rating
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the call the answers will make before you write a single question, such as which level to rebalance or which night to book. Put that decision in your prompt, and Emergent drafts questions that feed it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Send the survey within an hour of the session ending, and ask about that session rather than the whole game. Ask where each player got stuck tonight, while the level and the moment are still fresh in mind.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Use the same 5-point scale for every difficulty or fun rating, and say which end is hardest. A level rated 4 then means the same thing on build 14 and build 15, and levels compare side by side.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pew Research Center notes that even small wording differences can substantially affect the answers people provide. Ask how hard level 9 was, not whether it was too hard, which tells the player the answer you expect.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pew Research Center also notes that the order in which questions are asked can influence how people respond. Ask for the ratings first, then end on one open question about what the player would change.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the survey to 3 players before the full group, and watch for any question that two of them read differently or skip. Reword it with a follow-up prompt, then send the survey to everyone else.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Tell players what their answers changed, like the extra moves on a level or the new night on the schedule. Post it where they will see it before the next survey goes out, in the same channel the link came through.
fields.hero_prompt: Build game survey questions for my studio's playtest that ask testers to rate each level's difficulty on a 5-point scale.

faq_plan.a: Game survey questions ask players about a game they played or want to play: how hard a level felt, which night suits game night, or what they want from a campaign. Hosts also use the answers to build survey says party boards.

faq_plan.q: How do I create game survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Describe the game and what you plan to change based on the results, and Emergent's AI survey builder drafts the questions with their skip logic and a results table. Change any question with a follow-up prompt, then share the link when the session ends.

faq_plan.q: What game survey questions should a playtest ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask which level stopped each player, how hard every level they reached felt on a 5-point scale, and whether they would keep playing. Leave out levels a player never reached. Close with one open question about what they would change first.

faq_plan.q: How do you make game survey questions fun to answer?
faq_plan.a: Keep each question short, offer playful answer choices where the stakes are low, and let players tap through the survey on a phone. For a party crowd, mix a few funny survey questions in between the ones whose answers you need.

faq_plan.q: How many game survey questions are too many?
faq_plan.a: After a single session, more than 10 is too many: keep the survey short enough to finish before the next match. A deeper playtest can run longer when each question feeds a decision. Emergent puts no response cap on surveys, and every tester in the group can answer.

faq_plan.q: Should game survey questions be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when an honest answer could feel personal, like topics a tabletop player wants kept out of the game. Keep names when you need to follow up, such as asking one playtester to replay a level while you watch.

faq_plan.q: Should game survey questions use rating scales or yes or no answers?
faq_plan.a: Use rating scales for anything with degrees, like difficulty or fun, and yes or no for facts, like whether a player finished the level. A yes no questions survey is faster to answer but hides how close a player came.

faq_plan.q: How do you turn game survey questions into a survey says party game?
faq_plan.a: Send open questions to the group a week ahead and merge near matches. Then count how many people gave each answer. Put the top answers on the board in order, with the count beside each. Emergent builds the survey and the tally board from one prompt.

faq_plan.q: What game survey questions belong in a tabletop session zero?
faq_plan.a: Ask each player to rank what they want most at the table, how often they can play, and which topics they want left out. Ask for character ideas last. The game master can then tie them into the first arc.

faq_plan.q: Can game survey questions test a new game idea before it is built?
faq_plan.a: Yes, with a concept testing survey: show players a one-paragraph pitch and a mockup screen, then ask how likely they are to play it on a 5-point scale. Use the same questions for every pitch. Each answer is saved in a database you own, with its pitch attached.

plan.angle: The top 10 for game survey questions is a mix with no clear winner: Reddit and Facebook threads, a Scribd questionnaire about video game habits, a Survio template on video and board game habits, and a PlaytestCloud list of playtest questions for match-3 games, plus fan posts for survey-says style party games.
